classification.difficultyReason: Use the common-chord theorem to identify two right triangles with a shared half-chord, calculate their centre-to-chord distances and add them, simplifying the exact surd.

content.prompt:
In this diagram, radius $AD=5\text{ mm}$, radius $BD=12\text{ mm}$ and chord $CD=8\text{ mm}$.
Find the exact length of $AB$, in surd form.

spec.description: Smaller circle centred at A on the left and larger circle centred at B on the right. C and D are their upper and lower intersections. Solid line AB crosses dashed common chord CD; all four radii to the intersections are dashed.
spec.mathematics: AD = AC = 5 mm; BD = BC = 12 mm; CD = 8 mm. The centres lie on opposite sides of the common chord. Coordinates derive from half-chord 4 mm, with distances 3 mm and 8√2 mm from the common chord.
spec.answerVisibility: The diagram contains only the source labels A, B, C and D. No numerical result or added midpoint label appears.

answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the intersection of $AB$ and $CD$. The line joining the centres bisects the common chord at right angles, so $DM=4\text{ mm}$.
$$\begin{aligned}AM^2&=AD^2-DM^2\\AM^2&=5^2-4^2=9\\AM&=3\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}BM^2&=BD^2-DM^2\\BM^2&=12^2-4^2=128\\BM&=8\sqrt{2}\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}AB&=AM+BM\\AB&=(3+8\sqrt{2})\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$$
